title: Construction of a machine learning model for dual-region typing of norovirus RdRp and VP1 based on genomic k-mer features
abstract: Norovirus (NoV), a major global acute gastroenteritis pathogen, has high genetic diversity. Developing precise, rapid typing methods is crucial for epidemic control and vaccine development. Thus, this study develops a machine learning tool based on Norovirus genomic k-mer (length-k nucleotide fragments) features. It enables rapid, accurate dual-region typing of RdRp (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) and VP1 (major capsid protein) without alignment or segmentation. Using k-mer frequency features with k = 11, the MurmurHash3 algorithm maps the features to a 220-dimensional space and constructs a hash feature table. A random forest model comprising 500 decision trees is then used. Each tree randomly selects 20 features during node splitting. The model is trained and evaluated using a bootstrap sampling strategy (80% training and 20% out-of-bag estimation), and prediction confidence intervals are outputted. The typing accuracy rates for the RdRp region and VP1 region reached 97.6% and 99.3%, respectively. Analysis of precision, recall, and F1-score for each genotype in the test set showed that all metrics for the 40 RdRp genotypes and 34 VP1 genotypes were ≥ 0.9. Typing accuracy across all length intervals was ≥ 0.96. This study integrates machine learning and bioinformatics to develop a novel norovirus genome analysis tool. It enables precise genotyping despite multi-region interference and reveals hidden genomic information, supporting viral classification and tracing. The feature hashing and ensemble learning strategies overcome traditional dependencies on alignment and annotation, offering a universal, efficient, scalable framework for viral genome identification.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 使用引导抽样策略(80% 训练和 20% 袋外估计)对模型进行训练和评估,并输出预测置信区间。所提供的证据并未报告影响研究普遍性的具体限制或偏见。

abstract: Shellfish harbour emerging enteric viruses including sapovirus that are often not the main target for routine shellfish safety screening. Thus, the present investigation aimed at assessing the occurrence of sapovirus in 2450 shellfish samples using standard procedures and random-intercept logistic-regression modelling. The overall prevalence of shellfish-borne sapovirus was 17.14% (95% CI: 8.95-30.34). Sapovirus prevalence in shellfish was significantly different (p ≤ 0.0005) by shellfish type, family, genus, species, RNA extraction, nation and continent. Cockles (Cardiidae) showed the highest pooled sapovirus prevalence (∼26%), followed by clams (∼13%) and oysters (∼11). Among species, Perna spp had high-pooled sapovirus rate (66.5%), while Crassostrea gigas had 14%. Also, Sapovirus prevalence in shellfish was highest in Spain (35.8%), Brazil (25.3%), Italy (18.2%) and Japan (17.2%). By continent, South America (25.3%) and Europe (14.3%), pooled sapovirus rates in shellfish exceeded Asia (10.31%) and Africa (11.6%). The study identified detection methods and RNA extraction kits (as significant moderators) affect the ability to detect and accurately determine sapovirus prevalence (p≈0.05) in shellfish. Among 9 factors tested, nation and detection assays moderated sapovirus prevalence in shellfish significantly. Notably, shellfish species, genus, nation, kit, continent, family, detection assay, shellfish type, viral quality control, year, and sample size explained 67.27%, 56.93%, 55.48%, 43.51%, 38.92%, 35.89%, 28.14%, 23.36%, 18.06%, 4.74%, and 1.81%, respectively of the true variance in sapovirus pooled prevalence in shellfish. In conclusion, this study reveals that sapovirus contamination of shellfish is common. The pooled sapovirus prevalence in shellfish, with especially high rates in certain bivalves and locales, highlights sapovirus as a shellfish safety concern on par with norovirus. The findings underscore the importance of including sapovirus in routine shellfish monitoring and shellfish-linked outbreak investigations, complementing norovirus surveillance.

abstract_zh: 贝类含有新出现的肠道病毒,包括沙波病毒,这些病毒通常不是常规贝类安全筛查的主要目标。因此,本研究旨在使用标准程序和随机截取逻辑回归模型评估 2450 个贝类样本中沙波病毒的发生情况。贝类沙波病毒的总体 患病率 为 17.14% (95% CI: 8.95-30.34)。贝类中的沙波病毒 患病率 因贝类类型、科、属、种、RNA 提取、国家和大陆的不同而存在显着差异 (p ≤ 0.0005)。鸟蛤(Cardiidae)显示出最高的混合沙波病毒 患病率 (∼26%),其次是蛤 (∼13%) 和牡蛎 (∼11)。在物种中,珍珠贝的混合沙波病毒率较高(66.5%),而巨牡蛎为14%。此外,贝类中沙波病毒 患病率 最高的国家是西班牙(35.8%)、巴西(25.3%)、意大利(18.2%)和日本(17.2%)。按大陆划分,南美洲(25.3%)和欧洲(14.3%),贝类中沙波病毒的总比率超过亚洲(10.31%)和非洲(11.6%)。该研究确定检测方法和 RNA 提取试剂盒(作为重要调节剂)会影响贝类中检测和准确确定沙波病毒 患病率 (p≈0.05) 的能力。在测试的 9 个因素中,国家和检测分析显着调节了贝类中的沙波病毒 患病率。值得注意的是,贝类物种、属、国家、试剂盒、大陆、科、检测分析、贝类类型、病毒质量控制、年份和样本量解释了 67.27%、56.93%、55.48%、43.51%、38.92%、35.89%、28.14%、23.36%、18.06%、4.74% 和贝类中沙波病毒混合 患病率 的真实方差分别为 1.81%。总之,这项研究表明贝类的沙波病毒污染很常见。贝类中混合的沙波病毒 患病率 在某些双壳类和场所中的比率特别高,这表明沙波病毒与 诺如病毒 一样是贝类安全问题。研究结果强调了将沙波病毒纳入常规贝类监测和贝类相关 暴发 调查的重要性,以补充 诺如病毒 监测。

title: Norovirus outbreaks: maintaining infection prevention standards in community nursing
abstract: This article explores the evolving evidence surrounding norovirus outbreaks, considers lessons learned since the COVID-19 pandemic and discusses practical implications for community nursing practice in light of current UK guidance and infection prevention standards.

title: Optimization and Miniaturization of a Human Intestinal Organoid Neutralization Assay for Evaluating Human Norovirus Antibody Responses.
abstract: Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are the principal etiological agents of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide. While conventional 96-well human intestinal organoid (HIO) neutralization assays provide a physiologically relevant assessment of neutralizing antibody (nAb) responses, sample volume requirements (50μL for 96 wells vs. 12.5μL serum for 384 wells per titration) and 96-well plate capacity limit the application for large-scale clinical and vaccine studies. Here, we describe the development of a miniaturized 384-well HIO neutralization assay for nAb responses to HuNoV. Sera from a phase 2b trial of a bivalent GI.1 and consensus GII.4 virus-like particle norovirus vaccine candidate demonstrated high concordance in nAb responses to the predominant GII.4 Sydney variant between conventional 96-well and miniaturized 384-well assay formats (r= 0.95). Further, a strong correlation between nAb and histo-blood group antigen (HBGA)-blocking antibodies enables serum-sparing (25μL per titration, 4-fold reduction) norovirus immune profiling, supporting scalable deployment in large clinical trials. The 384-well plate neutralization assay maintains assay sensitivity, and concordance with the 96-well format increases scalability by allowing more samples per plate and reducing serum requirements.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to optimize and miniaturize a human intestinal organoid neutralization assay for evaluating human norovirus antibody responses, addressing the need for a scalable method for large-scale clinical and vaccine studies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved developing a miniaturized 384-well human intestinal organoid neutralization assay for nAb responses to HuNoV, using sera from a phase 2b trial of a bivalent GI.1 and GII.4 virus-like particle norovirus vaccine candidate.

title_zh: 用于评估人类 诺如病毒 抗体反应的人类肠道类器官中和测定的优化和小型化。
source_body_en: Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are the principal etiological agents of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide. While conventional 96-well human intestinal organoid (HIO) neutralization assays provide a physiologically relevant assessment of neutralizing antibody (nAb) responses, sample volume requirements (50μL for 96 wells vs. 12.5μL serum for 384 wells per titration) and 96-well plate capacity limit the application for large-scale clinical and vaccine studies. Here, we describe the development of a miniaturized 384-well HIO neutralization assay for nAb responses to HuNoV. Sera from a phase 2b trial of a bivalent GI.1 and consensus GII.4 virus-like particle norovirus vaccine candidate demonstrated high concordance in nAb responses to the predominant GII.4 Sydney variant between conventional 96-well and miniaturized 384-well assay formats (r= 0.95). Further, a strong correlation between nAb and histo-blood group antigen (HBGA)-blocking antibodies enables serum-sparing (25μL per titration, 4-fold reduction) norovirus immune profiling, supporting scalable deployment in large clinical trials. The 384-well plate neutralization assay maintains assay sensitivity, and concordance with the 96-well format increases scalability by allowing more samples per plate and reducing serum requirements.

title: mRNA encoding norovirus VP1 produces antigenically functional virus-like particles in vitro
abstract: Human norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide across all age groups, yet no licensed vaccine is available. The major capsid protein, VP1, self-assembles into highly immunogenic virus-like particles (VLPs) that have shown promise in clinical studies. Recently, mRNA has emerged as a compelling platform for norovirus vaccination. However, whether VP1-encoding mRNA can drive authentic VLP formation in human cells relevant to the vaccination environment has remained unknown. In this study, we used multiple human cell lines, including THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells, to model the post-vaccination environment. Transfection with norovirus GII.4 VP1 mRNA or lipid nanoparticle-formulated VP1 mRNA induced both intracellular and extracellular VP1 expression. Sucrose gradient purification and electron microscopy confirmed VLP assembly. These particles retained key antigenic and functional properties, including recognition by norovirus-specific antibodies in human serum and binding to histo-blood group antigens. Collectively, our findings provide direct evidence that VP1-encoding mRNA can generate structurally and functionally relevant norovirus VLPs in physiologically relevant human cell systems. These results strengthen the mechanistic rationale for mRNA-based norovirus vaccines and support their continued development.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of a licensed vaccine for human norovirus, a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide. The rationale was to investigate whether VP1-encoding mRNA can drive the formation of antigenically functional virus-like particles (VLPs) in human cells relevant to the vaccination environment.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study used multiple human cell lines, including THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells, to model the post-vaccination environment. No specific sample size or recruitment details were provided.
elements_en.methods: The study involved transfecting human cell lines with norovirus GII.4 VP1 mRNA or lipid nanoparticle-formulated VP1 mRNA to induce VP1 expression and VLP assembly. Sucrose gradient purification and electron microscopy were used to confirm VLP formation.
elements_en.main_results: Transfection with norovirus GII.4 VP1 mRNA or lipid nanoparticle-formulated VP1 mRNA induced both intracellular and extracellular VP1 expression. Sucrose gradient purification and electron microscopy confirmed VLP assembly. These particles retained key antigenic and functional properties, including recognition by norovirus-specific antibodies in human serum and binding to histo-blood group antigens.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as direct evidence that VP1-encoding mRNA can generate structurally and functionally relevant norovirus VLPs in physiologically relevant human cell systems, strengthening the mechanistic rationale for mRNA-based norovirus vaccines and supporting their continued development.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a mechanistic rationale for mRNA-based norovirus vaccines and support their continued development. These VLPs could be used for diagnostic, therapeutic, and vaccine development purposes.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a single norovirus strain (GII.4) and the need for further studies to confirm the generalizability of these findings to other norovirus strains and in vivo settings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the in vitro nature of the study.

title_zh: 编码 诺如病毒 VP1 的 mRNA 在体外产生具有抗原功能的病毒样颗粒
source_body_en: Human norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide across all age groups, yet no licensed vaccine is available. The major capsid protein, VP1, self-assembles into highly immunogenic virus-like particles (VLPs) that have shown promise in clinical studies. Recently, mRNA has emerged as a compelling platform for norovirus vaccination. However, whether VP1-encoding mRNA can drive authentic VLP formation in human cells relevant to the vaccination environment has remained unknown. In this study, we used multiple human cell lines, including THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells, to model the post-vaccination environment. Transfection with norovirus GII.4 VP1 mRNA or lipid nanoparticle-formulated VP1 mRNA induced both intracellular and extracellular VP1 expression. Sucrose gradient purification and electron microscopy confirmed VLP assembly. These particles retained key antigenic and functional properties, including recognition by norovirus-specific antibodies in human serum and binding to histo-blood group antigens. Collectively, our findings provide direct evidence that VP1-encoding mRNA can generate structurally and functionally relevant norovirus VLPs in physiologically relevant human cell systems. These results strengthen the mechanistic rationale for mRNA-based norovirus vaccines and support their continued development.

title: Multi-Virus Surveillance Across Diverse Freshwater Systems in Tehran, Iran.
abstract: Environmental surveillance of viral contaminants in water systems is an essential tool for assessing exposure risk and supporting early-warning frameworks for emerging infectious diseases. In this study, a comprehensive one-year surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 and six enteric viruses was conducted across diverse freshwater systems in Tehran, Iran - including rivers, wells, and traditional qanat (underground aqueduct) infrastructures. Water quality parameters (turbidity, pH, Total Dissolved Solids, nitrate) and fecal bacterial indicators (total coliforms, fecal coliforms, and E. coli) were also measured to contextualize viral contamination within a broader environmental risk framework. Between September 2020 and August 2021, a total of 118 water samples were collected and analyzed using quantitative molecular detection methods. Overall, 61 of 118 samples (51.7%) tested positive for at least one virus. Surface water (rivers) showed substantially higher contamination rates (80.3%; 53/66 samples) compared to groundwater (15.4%; 8/52 samples). Among groundwater sources, qanat systems were markedly more vulnerable than conventional wells, with 25.0% (6/24) of qanat samples testing positive versus only 7.1% (2/28) of well samples. This elevated contamination in qanats was dominated by rotavirus (5/6 positive qanat samples, detection rate 20.8%) and was associated with higher fecal bacterial loads (total coliform geometric mean: 245 MPN/100 mL in qanats vs. 28 MPN/100 mL in wells), consistent with the susceptibility of shallow horizontal collection channels to fecal infiltration. SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected in 34.8% of river samples and 3.9% of groundwater samples, with concentrations reaching 1.28 × 104 genome copies per liter (GC/L) in surface waters, demonstrating sustained fecal contamination across all seasons. The most prevalent viruses in river water were norovirus GII (45.5%), adenovirus (43.9%), rotavirus (42.4%), and norovirus GI (40.9%), with mean concentrations ranging from 1.26 × 102 to 3.76 × 103 GC/L. Hepatitis A and E viruses were not detected in any sample. Seasonal variation in viral detection was observed for enteric viruses, while SARS-CoV-2 and adenovirus showed year-round persistence. Strong correlations between fecal indicators and viral contamination (Spearman r = 0.61-0.63) support the use of bacterial monitoring as a cost-effective screening proxy. The results highlight the particular vulnerability of qanat systems and underscore the value of integrated environmental surveillance for water safety management in arid, water-stressed urban environments.

title_zh: 伊朗德黑兰多个淡水系统中出现多种病毒 监测。
source_body_en: Environmental surveillance of viral contaminants in water systems is an essential tool for assessing exposure risk and supporting early-warning frameworks for emerging infectious diseases. In this study, a comprehensive one-year surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 and six enteric viruses was conducted across diverse freshwater systems in Tehran, Iran - including rivers, wells, and traditional qanat (underground aqueduct) infrastructures. Water quality parameters (turbidity, pH, Total Dissolved Solids, nitrate) and fecal bacterial indicators (total coliforms, fecal coliforms, and E. coli) were also measured to contextualize viral contamination within a broader environmental risk framework. Between September 2020 and August 2021, a total of 118 water samples were collected and analyzed using quantitative molecular detection methods. Overall, 61 of 118 samples (51.7%) tested positive for at least one virus. Surface water (rivers) showed substantially higher contamination rates (80.3%; 53/66 samples) compared to groundwater (15.4%; 8/52 samples). Among groundwater sources, qanat systems were markedly more vulnerable than conventional wells, with 25.0% (6/24) of qanat samples testing positive versus only 7.1% (2/28) of well samples. This elevated contamination in qanats was dominated by rotavirus (5/6 positive qanat samples, detection rate 20.8%) and was associated with higher fecal bacterial loads (total coliform geometric mean: 245 MPN/100 mL in qanats vs. 28 MPN/100 mL in wells), consistent with the susceptibility of shallow horizontal collection channels to fecal infiltration. SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected in 34.8% of river samples and 3.9% of groundwater samples, with concentrations reaching 1.28 × 104 genome copies per liter (GC/L) in surface waters, demonstrating sustained fecal contamination across all seasons. The most prevalent viruses in river water were norovirus GII (45.5%), adenovirus (43.9%), rotavirus (42.4%), and norovirus GI (40.9%), with mean concentrations ranging from 1.26 × 102 to 3.76 × 103 GC/L. Hepatitis A and E viruses were not detected in any sample. Seasonal variation in viral detection was observed for enteric viruses, while SARS-CoV-2 and adenovirus showed year-round persistence. Strong correlations between fecal indicators and viral contamination (Spearman r = 0.61-0.63) support the use of bacterial monitoring as a cost-effective screening proxy. The results highlight the particular vulnerability of qanat systems and underscore the value of integrated environmental surveillance for water safety management in arid, water-stressed urban environments.
abstract_zh: 水系统中病毒污染物的环境 监测 是评估暴露风险和支持新发传染病预警框架的重要工具。在这项研究中,对伊朗德黑兰的不同淡水系统(包括河流、水井和传统坎儿井(地下渡槽)基础设施)进行了为期一年的 SARS-CoV-2 和六种肠道病毒综合 监测 调查。还测量了水质参数(浊度、pH、总溶解固体、硝酸盐)和粪便细菌指标(总大肠菌群、粪便大肠菌群和大肠杆菌),以便在更广泛的环境风险框架内了解病毒污染情况。2020年9月至2021年8月期间,共采集118份水样,并采用定量分子检测方法进行分析。总体而言,118 个样本中有 61 个(51.7%)检测出至少一种病毒呈阳性。与地下水(15.4%;8/52 个样本)相比,地表水(河流)的污染率(80.3%;53/66 个样本)要高得多。在地下水源中,坎儿井系统明显比常规水井更脆弱,25.0% (6/24) 的坎儿井样本检测呈阳性,而井样本中只有 7.1% (2/28) 呈阳性。坎儿井中污染的增加主要是轮状病毒(5/6 坎儿井样本呈阳性,检出率为 20.8%),并且与较高的粪便细菌负荷相关(总大肠菌几何平均值:坎儿井中为 245 MPN/100 mL,孔中为 28 MPN/100 mL),这与浅水平收集通道对粪便渗透的敏感性一致。在 34.8% 的河流样本和 3.9% 的地下水样本中检测到 SARS-CoV-2 RNA,地表水中的浓度达到每升 1.28 × 104 基因组 拷贝 (GC/L),表明粪便在所有季节都存在持续污染。河水中最常见的病毒是诺如病毒 GII (45.5%)、腺病毒(43.9%)、轮状病毒(42.4%)和诺如病毒 GI (40.9%),平均浓度范围为1.26 × 102至3.76 × 103 GC/L。在任何样本中均未检测到甲型和戊型肝炎病毒。肠道病毒的病毒检测存在季节性变化,而 SARS-CoV-2 和腺病毒则全年持续存在。粪便指标和病毒污染之间的强相关性(Spearman r = 0.61-0.63)支持使用细菌监测作为具有成本效益的筛查代理。研究结果凸显了坎儿井系统的特殊脆弱性,并强调了综合环境 监测 对于干旱、缺水城市环境中水安全管理的价值。

title: Etiology and incidence of diarrhea requiring hospitalization in children under 5 years of age in 31 low- and middle-income countries: Findings from the Global Pediatric Diarrhea Surveillance network, 2017-2022.
abstract: Diarrhea remains a leading cause of child morbidity and mortality. Improved and ongoing estimates of the etiology of hospitalized pediatric diarrhea in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are needed to help prioritize and evaluate the use of existing and upcoming vaccines and interventions. The Global Pediatric Diarrhea Surveillance (GPDS) network is a World Health Organization (WHO)-coordinated public health surveillance network investigating the etiology of hospitalized diarrhea among children aged <5 years in LMICs. The GPDS network enrolls children hospitalized with diarrhea at 38 sentinel surveillance sites in 31 LMICs. Randomly selected stool specimens were tested by TaqMan Array Card quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) for 16 pathogens associated with diarrhea. We estimated pathogen-specific attributable fractions (AFs) and incidence of diarrheal hospitalizations at the global, regional, and country levels during 3 time periods: 2017-2018, 2019-2020, and 2021-2022, with a focus on the most recent results. During 2017-2022, the GPDS network enrolled 70,750 children aged <5 years hospitalized with diarrhea, of which 16,458 (23.3%) were randomly selected for qPCR testing. The most prevalent pathogen detected, regardless of quantity or modeled etiologic attribution, was rotavirus (weighted prevalence 30.4%), followed by adenovirus 40/41 (19.1%), norovirus (17.9%), Shigella (14.1%), and Campylobacter jejuni/coli (8.6%). Overall, in 2017-2022, rotavirus was the leading etiology globally (AF 32.5%; 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 27.4, 37.6), followed by Shigella (9.8%; 8.4, 11.3), adenovirus 40/41 (8.6%; 6.3, 10.8) and norovirus (6.7%; 5.6, 7.7). Over time, rotavirus consistently declined from an AF of 36.7% (95% CI: 28.7, 46.7) in 2017-2018 to 26.7% (20.7, 34.1) in 2021-2022. Norovirus AF increased slightly from 6.2% (4.7, 7.7) in 2017-2018 to 7.3% (5.0, 9.2) in 2021-2022. Global Shigella burden remained stable, and adenovirus 40/41 demonstrated significant volatility, peaking globally in 2019-2020 (11.9%; 5.9, 17.5). In 2021-2022, rotavirus was the leading cause of hospitalized diarrhea in 6 of 9 geographic groupings, norovirus predominated in Central and South America, and Shigella was the leading etiology in South Asia. In the subset of countries that had introduced rotavirus vaccine, the leading etiologies in 2021-2022 were rotavirus (18.4%; 15.8, 21.5) and Shigella (16.4%; 11.8, 21.1). In 2021-2022, rotavirus had the highest attributable incidence of hospitalized diarrhea in children (2.3 per 1,000 child-years; 1.8, 3.0), followed by Shigella (0.9; 0.7, 1.1), norovirus (0.6; 0.4, 0.8) and adenovirus 40/41 (0.6; 0.4, 0.8). Despite the widespread use of rotavirus vaccines, rotavirus remained the leading cause of severe diarrhea among children aged <5 years in LMICs globally. However, the proportion of pediatric diarrhea attributable to rotavirus consistently declined from 2017-2018-2021-2022, and there were notable differences in the distribution of diarrheal etiologies between regions and across time periods. Shigella, norovirus, and enteric adenoviruses were also associated with a substantial burden of disease. Improving the efficacy and coverage of rotavirus vaccination and prioritizing interventions against other enteric pathogens could further reduce diarrhea morbidity and mortality.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the etiology of hospitalized diarrhea in children under 5 years in 31 low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) from 2017 to 2022. It highlights that norovirus was the third most prevalent pathogen, with an attributable fraction (AF) of 6.7% (5.6, 7.7) globally. The AF for norovirus increased slightly over time, from 6.2% (4.7, 7.7) in 2017-2018 to 7.3% (5.0, 9.2) in 2021-2022. The study also notes that rotavirus remained the leading cause of severe diarrhea in LMICs, despite vaccine introduction, and that there were regional and temporal variations in the distribution of pathogens. These findings suggest the need for improved rotavirus vaccination and targeted interventions against other enteric pathogens to reduce diarrhea-related morbidity and mortality.

title_zh: 31 个低收入和中等收入国家 5 岁以下儿童需要住院治疗的腹泻的病因和 发病率:来自全球小儿腹泻 发病率 网络的调查结果,2017-2022 年。
source_body_en: Diarrhea remains a leading cause of child morbidity and mortality. Improved and ongoing estimates of the etiology of hospitalized pediatric diarrhea in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are needed to help prioritize and evaluate the use of existing and upcoming vaccines and interventions. The Global Pediatric Diarrhea Surveillance (GPDS) network is a World Health Organization (WHO)-coordinated public health surveillance network investigating the etiology of hospitalized diarrhea among children aged <5 years in LMICs. The GPDS network enrolls children hospitalized with diarrhea at 38 sentinel surveillance sites in 31 LMICs. Randomly selected stool specimens were tested by TaqMan Array Card quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) for 16 pathogens associated with diarrhea. We estimated pathogen-specific attributable fractions (AFs) and incidence of diarrheal hospitalizations at the global, regional, and country levels during 3 time periods: 2017-2018, 2019-2020, and 2021-2022, with a focus on the most recent results. During 2017-2022, the GPDS network enrolled 70,750 children aged <5 years hospitalized with diarrhea, of which 16,458 (23.3%) were randomly selected for qPCR testing. The most prevalent pathogen detected, regardless of quantity or modeled etiologic attribution, was rotavirus (weighted prevalence 30.4%), followed by adenovirus 40/41 (19.1%), norovirus (17.9%), Shigella (14.1%), and Campylobacter jejuni/coli (8.6%). Overall, in 2017-2022, rotavirus was the leading etiology globally (AF 32.5%; 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 27.4, 37.6), followed by Shigella (9.8%; 8.4, 11.3), adenovirus 40/41 (8.6%; 6.3, 10.8) and norovirus (6.7%; 5.6, 7.7). Over time, rotavirus consistently declined from an AF of 36.7% (95% CI: 28.7, 46.7) in 2017-2018 to 26.7% (20.7, 34.1) in 2021-2022. Norovirus AF increased slightly from 6.2% (4.7, 7.7) in 2017-2018 to 7.3% (5.0, 9.2) in 2021-2022. Global Shigella burden remained stable, and adenovirus 40/41 demonstrated significant volatility, peaking globally in 2019-2020 (11.9%; 5.9, 17.5). In 2021-2022, rotavirus was the leading cause of hospitalized diarrhea in 6 of 9 geographic groupings, norovirus predominated in Central and South America, and Shigella was the leading etiology in South Asia. In the subset of countries that had introduced rotavirus vaccine, the leading etiologies in 2021-2022 were rotavirus (18.4%; 15.8, 21.5) and Shigella (16.4%; 11.8, 21.1). In 2021-2022, rotavirus had the highest attributable incidence of hospitalized diarrhea in children (2.3 per 1,000 child-years; 1.8, 3.0), followed by Shigella (0.9; 0.7, 1.1), norovirus (0.6; 0.4, 0.8) and adenovirus 40/41 (0.6; 0.4, 0.8). Despite the widespread use of rotavirus vaccines, rotavirus remained the leading cause of severe diarrhea among children aged <5 years in LMICs globally. However, the proportion of pediatric diarrhea attributable to rotavirus consistently declined from 2017-2018-2021-2022, and there were notable differences in the distribution of diarrheal etiologies between regions and across time periods. Shigella, norovirus, and enteric adenoviruses were also associated with a substantial burden of disease. Improving the efficacy and coverage of rotavirus vaccination and prioritizing interventions against other enteric pathogens could further reduce diarrhea morbidity and mortality.

title: A Narrative Review of the Norovirus Burden in Closed and Semi-Closed Structural Settings
abstract: Noroviruses pose a major public health challenge in structurally closed or semi-closed settings where person-to-person contact, shared environment, and high-risk populations facilitate rapid transmission. This narrative review synthesizes epidemiological evidence on the burden of norovirus infection in closed and semi-closed settings, such as long-term care facilities (LTCFs), healthcare facilities, schools, childcare centers, and cruise ships, where norovirus transmission risk is elevated. Priority populations frequently experiencing high attack rates and patterns of key factors related to norovirus transmission are summarized for each context. Reported attack rates varied substantially both within and across settings, with elevated attack rates reported in LTCFs, healthcare facilities, childcare settings, and several other closed or semi-closed settings. Norovirus outbreaks are frequent and severe in closed and semi-closed settings, highlighting the need for targeted prevention and control measures in these contexts.

title_zh: 封闭和半封闭结构环境中 诺如病毒 负担的叙述回顾
source_body_en: Noroviruses pose a major public health challenge in structurally closed or semi-closed settings where person-to-person contact, shared environment, and high-risk populations facilitate rapid transmission. This narrative review synthesizes epidemiological evidence on the burden of norovirus infection in closed and semi-closed settings, such as long-term care facilities (LTCFs), healthcare facilities, schools, childcare centers, and cruise ships, where norovirus transmission risk is elevated. Priority populations frequently experiencing high attack rates and patterns of key factors related to norovirus transmission are summarized for each context. Reported attack rates varied substantially both within and across settings, with elevated attack rates reported in LTCFs, healthcare facilities, childcare settings, and several other closed or semi-closed settings. Norovirus outbreaks are frequent and severe in closed and semi-closed settings, highlighting the need for targeted prevention and control measures in these contexts.

title: Longitudinal Surface Water Viral Surveillance Following the 2024 Extreme Flood: One-Year Monitoring in Porto Alegre, Brazil.
abstract: Abstract Extreme flood events can overwhelm sanitation infrastructure and drive the widespread dispersal of viral pathogens into aquatic environments. In May 2024, Porto Alegre (southern Brazil) experienced an unprecedented flood that caused record-breaking overflow of the Guaíba hydrological system and prolonged urban inundation. Here we report a one-year longitudinal environmental viral surveillance study, comprising seven campaigns between May 2024 and April 2025. Surface waters were analyzed by RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2, norovirus genogroups I and II, hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis E virus (HEV). All five targets were detected simultaneously during the flood peak, reflecting widespread contamination possibly driven by sewage overflow and multi-site infrastructure failure. Thereafter, the number of targets detected per campaign was lower and fluctuating (two to four), tracing a transition from an initial multi-pathogen contamination pulse observed during the flood peak to persistent detection of viral genomic material in surface waters. SARS-CoV-2 was detected in every campaign, in a minority of sites in all campaigns except the last (C7, 14/22, 63.6%), where both detection frequency and viral load increased significantly ( p < 0.001 for both; median Ct 29.7 versus 36.8). HEV was detected only at the flood peak; norovirus GII was detected intermittently up to C6, without a significant temporal pattern ( p = 0.13); and norovirus GI was absent between C2 and C5, reappearing in C6 and C7. HAV detection increased significantly over the monitoring period (Cochran–Armitage p < 0.0005), temporally coincident with an officially declared hepatitis A outbreak. These findings demonstrate the value of longitudinal, multi-target environmental surveillance for capturing both the acute virological impact of extreme flooding and the persistent contamination dynamics that follow, pointing to chronic vulnerabilities in urban wastewater infrastructure that outlast the emergency.
authors: Luis Gustavo Dos Santos Da Silva

title_zh: 2024 年极端洪水后的纵向地表水病毒 监测:巴西阿雷格里港的一年监测。
source_body_en: Abstract Extreme flood events can overwhelm sanitation infrastructure and drive the widespread dispersal of viral pathogens into aquatic environments. In May 2024, Porto Alegre (southern Brazil) experienced an unprecedented flood that caused record-breaking overflow of the Guaíba hydrological system and prolonged urban inundation. Here we report a one-year longitudinal environmental viral surveillance study, comprising seven campaigns between May 2024 and April 2025. Surface waters were analyzed by RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2, norovirus genogroups I and II, hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis E virus (HEV). All five targets were detected simultaneously during the flood peak, reflecting widespread contamination possibly driven by sewage overflow and multi-site infrastructure failure. Thereafter, the number of targets detected per campaign was lower and fluctuating (two to four), tracing a transition from an initial multi-pathogen contamination pulse observed during the flood peak to persistent detection of viral genomic material in surface waters. SARS-CoV-2 was detected in every campaign, in a minority of sites in all campaigns except the last (C7, 14/22, 63.6%), where both detection frequency and viral load increased significantly ( p < 0.001 for both; median Ct 29.7 versus 36.8). HEV was detected only at the flood peak; norovirus GII was detected intermittently up to C6, without a significant temporal pattern ( p = 0.13); and norovirus GI was absent between C2 and C5, reappearing in C6 and C7. HAV detection increased significantly over the monitoring period (Cochran–Armitage p < 0.0005), temporally coincident with an officially declared hepatitis A outbreak. These findings demonstrate the value of longitudinal, multi-target environmental surveillance for capturing both the acute virological impact of extreme flooding and the persistent contamination dynamics that follow, pointing to chronic vulnerabilities in urban wastewater infrastructure that outlast the emergency.

title: EpiLinx - An interactive tool for establishing epidemiological links as part of national nosocomial outbreak investigation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections remain a major public health challenge worldwide. Effective surveillance requires timely identification of epidemiological links. Although electronic health records are widely used, their complexity often hinder rapid analysis in practice. We developed EpiLinx, a user-friendly tool that uses administrative patient data to support systematic investigation of suspected outbreaks in healthcare settings. The aim of this paper is to present EpiLinx and assess its usability against two real-life healthcare associated outbreaks. METHODS: EpiLinx is an R shiny application that identifies spatio-temporal overlaps between patients' hospital contacts in extensive datasets. It provides interactive tables and visualizations, including timelines and network diagrams, to support rapid data exploration. The software is designed to be generic with minimal data requirements to ensure accessibility for non-technical users. RESULTS: EpiLinx was applied to a Danish Enterobacter hormaechei outbreak and a British norovirus outbreak. In both cases, EpiLinx rapidly generated visualizations and network structures consistent with the conclusions of the original investigations. Analyses that previously required hours of manual data handling were completed within seconds. CONCLUSION: EpiLinx enables rapid and intuitive exploration of epidemiological links in large healthcare datasets, supporting more timely outbreak investigations. Its simplicity and minimal data requirements make it readily applicable in clinical practice, including for non-technical users. The approach is broadly applicable across settings where routinely collected administrative data are available. By improving transparency and accessibility in link assessment, EpiLinx has the potential to strengthen infection control in both clinical and public health contexts.

abstract_zh: 背景:医疗保健相关感染仍然是全球主要的公共卫生挑战。有效的监测需要及时识别流行病学联系。尽管电子健康记录被广泛使用,但其复杂性往往阻碍了实践中的快速分析。我们开发了 EpiLinx,这是一种用户友好的工具,它使用管理患者数据来支持医疗机构中可疑 暴发 的系统调查。本文的目的是介绍 EpiLinx 并评估其针对两个现实生活中的医疗保健相关 暴发 的可用性。方法:EpiLinx 是一款 R 闪亮应用程序,可识别大量数据集中患者医院联系人之间的时空重叠。它提供交互式表格和可视化,包括时间线和网络图,以支持快速数据探索。该软件设计为通用型,具有最少的数据要求,以确保非技术用户的可访问性。结果:EpiLinx 应用于丹麦霍马氏肠杆菌 暴发 和英国 诺如病毒 暴发。在这两种情况下,EpiLinx 都快速生成了与原始调查结论一致的可视化和网络结构。以前需要数小时的手动数据处理的分析在几秒钟内完成。结论:EpiLinx 能够快速、直观地探索大型医疗数据集中的流行病学联系,支持更及时的 暴发 调查。其简单性和最少的数据要求使其易于应用于临床实践,包括非技术用户。该方法广泛适用于可以获得常规收集的管理数据的环境。通过提高关联评估的透明度和可访问性,EpiLinx 有潜力加强临床和公共卫生环境中的感染控制。

title: Rotavirus Vaccines
abstract: Abstract Rotavirus remains a leading cause of severe gastroenteritis and child mortality worldwide, despite significant advances in vaccine development. Four WHO prequalified live-attenuated and orally administered vaccines are in use, with two additional vaccines licensed regionally. The development process faced challenges such as variability in efficacy across geographic regions and safety concerns like intussusception. Notably, the oral vaccines exhibit lower efficacy in low-resource settings due to several factors, including malnutrition, genetic heterogeneity, microbiome differences, coinfections, and potentially, the force of infection. Nevertheless, rotavirus vaccines have substantially reduced childhood gastroenteritis-associated global mortality, from approximately 500,000 deaths in 2006 to 185,000 in 2019, saving millions of life-years. Ongoing efforts focus on improving efficacy through innovative formulations, parenteral delivery, and enteric adjuvants, particularly for low-income countries where disease burden is highest. Vaccination programs have achieved remarkable success in high- and middle-income countries, with significant reductions in hospitalizations and indirect herd immunity effects. Continued research and equitable distribution are essential to overcome logistical challenges and enhance vaccine impact, aiming to further diminish the global childhood burden of rotavirus-related morbidity and mortality.

title: Climate Change, Waterborne Pathogens, and the Future of WASH
abstract: Climate change is altering hydrological cycles, water temperature, precipitation extremes, drought frequency, and infrastructure reliability, reshaping exposure to waterborne pathogens. This chapter examines how these changes affect bacteria, viruses, and protozoa, including Vibrio cholerae, pathogenic Escherichia coli, Salmonella, Campylobacter, norovirus, rotavirus, Cryptosporidium, and Giardia, and how failures across water, sanitation, and hygiene systems amplify risk. It integrates climate-resilient water and sanitation safety planning with digital microbiology, including online sensors, remote sensing, molecular diagnostics, metagenomics, wastewater surveillance, quantitative microbial risk assessment, and AI-based early warning. The future of WASH will depend on resilient infrastructure, inclusive governance, continuous microbial surveillance, locally calibrated predictive models, and rapid translation of environmental signals into preventive action.

title: Specific residues modulate the antiviral activity of the extracellular vesicle-derived effector SH3b domain from Lactobacillus johnsonii N6.2
abstract: Lactobacillus johnsonii N6.2-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) provide protection against murine norovirus (MNV-1) both in vitro and in vivo . Within the proteins enriched in EVs, the SH3b2 domain of Sdp was shown to be sufficient to recapitulate the antiviral effects shown by EVs. In this report, we compared the effects of six SH3b domains of Sdp and identified amino acids expected to be important for interactions with host proteins. We found that SH3b2 showed the highest activity in inducing NF-ĸB/AP-1 and IRF pathways in RAW macrophage reporter cell lines. Structure-guided site-directed mutagenesis of SH3b2 revealed residues in SH3b2 potentially responsible for interactions with host proteins. SH3b2-G501D had significantly lower stimulation of NF-ĸB/AP-1 and IRF pathways. In addition, SH3b2-G501D showed reduced IL10 and Oas1 mRNA levels, resulting in an impaired MNV-1 antiviral response in RAW 264.7 cells. mCherry fusions to SH3b2-G501D confirmed that the effects observed were not related to reduced uptake into macrophages, as quantified by confocal microscopy. Additionally, the role of the C-terminal linker sequence in Sh3b2, which is absent in SH3b6, in uptake or signaling in macrophages was evaluated. It was found that deletion of the C-terminal linker (SH3b2ΔC2 treatment) resulted in reduced promoter activity, while SH3b6::C2 partially regained function through restoration of uptake in macrophages. These results indicate that the C-terminal linker plays an important role in internalization by macrophages. We propose that once internalized, SH3b2 mimics eukaryotic SH3 domains involved in signal transduction to activate the cellular innate immune response in macrophages.

title: Caracterització de virus entèrics en aigües residuals i regenerades
abstract: [ES] Los virus son patógenos relevantes para la salud pública, con capacidad de provocar enfermedades agudas, crónicas e incluso letales. Los alimentos y el agua suponen dos de las fuentes de transmisión de virus más importantes, principalmente de virus transmitidos a través de la ruta fecal-oral, conocidos como virus entéricos. En el contexto del ciclo hidrológico urbano, las aguas residuales domésticas pueden contener virus excretados en heces, que, cuando no se utilizan los procesos de regeneración de agua residual correctos, pueden llegar a los efluentes de las estaciones de tratamiento de agua residual (EDAR). La reutilización de estas aguas regeneradas contaminadas para riego agrícola o usos industriales plantea riesgos potenciales de diseminación vírica. Es por ello que la vigilancia virológica en aguas regeneradas es esencial para evaluar la eficacia de los procesos de depuración y mitigar el riesgo de transmisión viral a través de la cadena alimentaria o el ambiente, especialmente cuando dicho agua se destina al riego de cultivos o procesos industriales susceptibles de contaminación biológica. El objetivo de este estudio se centra en comparar la presencia y diversidad de virus entéricos (norovirus humanos, virus de las hepatitis A y E, rotavirus y enterovirus) en las aguas de entrada y salida de cuatro estaciones depuradoras, antes y después de diferentes tratamientos de regeneración, mediante técnicas de biología molecular (qPCR) y secuenciación masiva. Esto permitirá tanto conocer las concentraciones virales en los influentes y los genotipos circulantes como la capacidad de las EDAR para la eliminación de virus.

abstract_zh: [ES] 病毒与公共健康有关,具有挑衅性、历史性和包括性的能力。食物和水的供应是病毒传播的重要因素,病毒通过粪便-口腔传播的原理,是肠道病毒的传播途径。在城市水环境背景下,国内水残留物中含有病毒排泄物,因此,我们无法利用残留水校正再生过程,将水残留物和水残留物排放物 (EDAR) 排出。重新利用农业或工业植物中污染的水,以消除病毒传播的潜力。病毒预防和水再生是对净化过程的功效和减轻病毒传播以及食品和环境中的病毒传播进行重要评估,特别是对栽培过程的目的而言工业易受生物污染。该研究的目的是比较肠道病毒的存在和多样性(诺如病毒 人类、甲型肝炎病毒和戊型肝炎病毒、轮状病毒和肠道病毒)以及四肢的水和唾液,以及不同病原体的前奏和设计再生、分子生物学中间技术 (qPCR) 和维护。允许病毒浓度与 EDAR 的影响力和基因循环能力一起消除病毒。

full_text: AbstractIntroductionHuman parechovirus is a common pathogen causing respiratory and gastroenterological symptoms. full_text_sections.other: IntroductionHuman parechovirus (HPeV) is a common pathogen belonging to the family of picornaviridae, which also includes other virus types such as enterovirus or poliovirus and is associated especially with respiratory and gastrointestinal symptoms. In most cases, infection is mild, and the majority of children have been infected by the age of three years (1). Among young infants presenting with fever without an identifiable source upon initial clinical assessment, HPeV is later detected in 6%–15% of cases (2, 3). Several studies have reported a male predominance, with male infants accounting for 56%–91% of cases (4).Among the 19 recognised HPeV genotypes, types 1 and 3 in particular have been associated with more severe disease (5). HPeV type 3 is the genotype predominantly involved in severe infections, especially among infants younger than three months. Whereas the clinical spectrum of parechovirus infection ranges from asymptomatic infection to rare cases of encephalitis, severe manifestations occur predominantly in this age group (4–7). Fever is the most common clinical manifestation, occurring in 80%–100% of reported cases. Erythema is reported in 20%–60% of cases, whereas seizures occur in 3%–65%. Other manifestations include diarrhea, respiratory symptoms, irritability, poor feeding and tachycardia (4).Laboratory abnormalities are generally mild and non-specific, with leukopenia being particularly common in infants younger than three months. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings are usually unremarkable, and pleocytosis is typically absent. Cranial ultrasonography is generally normal. In patients with neurological involvement, MRI is the imaging modality of choice and may reveal characteristic white-matter abnormalities (4).In a British study by Braccio et al., 83% of patients with HPeV infection admitted to a paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) were younger than one year, and 40% presented with neurological manifestations. Neurological complications were particularly common among infants younger than three months, occurring in 46% of this age group. Invasive mechanical ventilation was required in 77% of patients admitted to the PICU. The mortality rate was approximately 8% (8). In other studies among infants with severe neurological manifestations of HPeV type 3 infection, reported mortality rates range from 1.6% to 6% (5).Here, we report an exceptionally severe case of HPeV infection in a young infant. Case descriptionMedical historyA two-week-old male infant presented to our emergency department with fever. His stools had been slightly looser than usual; however, oral intake remained adequate. Several family members were experiencing symptoms of an upper respiratory tract infection at the time of presentation. He had been born by uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery at 37 + 2 weeks of gestation, with a birth weight of 3,300 g. Maternal group B streptococcus colonisation status was unknown.
